blocks.text: The Method of Śakti: or, how to think your way out of the absolute bloody mess that thinking got you into.
blocks.directed: The Method of Śakti: or, how to think your way out of the absolute bloody mess that thinking got you into.

blocks.text: You recognise the entire universe as the expression of your own divine consciousness, and that’s that.
blocks.directed: You recognise the entire universe as the expression of your own divine consciousness, and that’s that.

blocks.text: Some of you are still thinking.
blocks.directed: Some of you are still thinking.

blocks.text: You’ve been thinking your entire life.
blocks.directed: You’ve been thinking your entire life.

blocks.text: You’ve constructed this enormous conceptual prison, furnished it with beliefs, decorated it with anxieties, and now you’re sitting in the middle of it going:
blocks.directed: [short pause] You’ve constructed this enormous conceptual prison, furnished it with beliefs, decorated it with anxieties, and now you’re sitting in the middle of it going:

blocks.text: “Well, I suppose this is who I am.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Well, I suppose this is who I am.”

blocks.text: Because Śakti has got another trick up her sleeve.
blocks.directed: Because Śakti has got another trick up her sleeve.

blocks.text: We’re going to use your own thinking to destroy the thinking that’s keeping you bound.
blocks.directed: We’re going to use your own thinking to destroy the thinking that’s keeping you bound.

blocks.text:
1. The problem is what you’ve convinced yourself you are
Let’s begin.
blocks.directed:
1. The problem is what you’ve convinced yourself you are
Let’s begin.

blocks.text: You regard yourself as a captive, a limited being.
blocks.directed: You regard yourself as a captive, a limited being.

blocks.text: Because of the power of vikalpa.
blocks.directed: Because of the power of vikalpa.

blocks.text: You’re constantly telling yourself what you are.
blocks.directed: You’re constantly telling yourself what you are.

blocks.text: And you’ve repeated these ideas so often that you’ve started taking them for reality itself.
blocks.directed: And you’ve repeated these ideas so often that you’ve started taking them for reality itself.

blocks.text: The very power that constructs these limiting convictions can also construct their opposites.
blocks.directed: The very power that constructs these limiting convictions can also construct their opposites.

blocks.text: And when it arises with sufficient force, it can shatter the conceptual understanding responsible for perpetuating saṃsāra.
blocks.directed: And when it arises with sufficient force, it can shatter the conceptual understanding responsible for perpetuating saṃsāra.

blocks.text: It crushes the thought that causes bondage.
blocks.directed: It crushes the thought that causes bondage.

blocks.text: Imagine you’ve spent your entire life convinced that there’s a gigantic tiger waiting outside your bedroom.
blocks.directed: Imagine you’ve spent your entire life convinced that there’s a gigantic tiger waiting outside your bedroom.

blocks.text: Every morning you wake up, look at the door, and think:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Every morning you wake up, look at the door, and think:

blocks.text: Then someone who actually understands the situation comes along and explains that there’s no tiger.
blocks.directed: Then someone who actually understands the situation comes along and explains that there’s no tiger.

blocks.text: And eventually the false conviction collapses.
blocks.directed: And eventually the false conviction collapses.

blocks.text: Now, have you physically removed a tiger?
blocks.directed: Now, have you physically removed a tiger?

blocks.text: The correction doesn’t manufacture freedom. It removes a mistaken conviction.
blocks.directed: The correction doesn’t manufacture freedom. It removes a mistaken conviction.

2. So what exactly should I be thinking?
Excellent question.
blocks.directed:
2. So what exactly should I be thinking?
Excellent question.

blocks.text: Beyond every limited principle of reality — even the principle called Śiva when considered as one member of the hierarchy of tattvas — lies the supreme, unrestricted reality.
blocks.directed: Beyond every limited principle of reality — even the principle called Śiva when considered as one member of the hierarchy of tattvas — lies the supreme, unrestricted reality.

blocks.text: And this isn’t some abstract substance sitting somewhere beyond the universe.
blocks.directed: And this isn’t some abstract substance sitting somewhere beyond the universe.

blocks.text: It’s the very ground of everything that exists.
blocks.directed: It’s the very ground of everything that exists.

blocks.text: The foundation upon which the ordering of reality rests.
blocks.directed: The foundation upon which the ordering of reality rests.

blocks.text: It’s the vitality of the universe.
blocks.directed: It’s the vitality of the universe.

blocks.text: That by which the entire cosmos lives.
blocks.directed: That by which the entire cosmos lives.

blocks.text: And now comes the important bit.
blocks.directed: And now comes the important bit.

blocks.text: Not merely something I belong to.
blocks.directed: Not merely something I belong to.

blocks.text: Not something I might eventually meet when I die.
blocks.directed: Not something I might eventually meet when I die.

blocks.text: I transcend the universe, and I am the Self of the universe.
blocks.directed: I transcend the universe, and I am the Self of the universe.

blocks.text: Because if you’re only the universe, you’ve limited yourself to its forms.
blocks.directed: Because if you’re only the universe, you’ve limited yourself to its forms.

blocks.text: And if you’re only beyond the universe, you’ve excluded the very manifestations of your own consciousness.
blocks.directed: And if you’re only beyond the universe, you’ve excluded the very manifestations of your own consciousness.

blocks.text: The universe appears within your nature, without exhausting what you are.
blocks.directed: The universe appears within your nature, without exhausting what you are.

3. Why doesn’t everyone recognise this?
Now you might be wondering:

Now you might be wondering:

blocks.text: “Abhinava, mate, if it’s that straightforward, why doesn’t everyone just understand it?”

blocks.text: Because not everyone possesses the discernment necessary to arrive at this understanding.
blocks.directed: Because not everyone possesses the discernment necessary to arrive at this understanding.

blocks.text: And some people are positively determined not to.
blocks.directed: And some people are positively determined not to.

blocks.text: They’ve become attached to limited doctrines.
blocks.directed: They’ve become attached to limited doctrines.

blocks.text: They’ve got their particular scriptures, particular conceptions of divinity, particular explanations of reality.
blocks.directed: They’ve got their particular scriptures, particular conceptions of divinity, particular explanations of reality.

blocks.text: And they’re absolutely delighted with them.
blocks.directed: And they’re absolutely delighted with them.
[short pause] “NO, THIS is the highest truth.”

blocks.text: And while they’re all having a tremendous argument, the unrestricted consciousness within which they’re arguing goes entirely unrecognised.
blocks.directed: And while they’re all having a tremendous argument, the unrestricted consciousness within which they’re arguing goes entirely unrecognised.

blocks.text: Now, Abhinavagupta makes a rather pointed criticism of Vaiṣṇava and other traditions here.
blocks.directed: Now, Abhinavagupta makes a rather pointed criticism of Vaiṣṇava and other traditions here.

blocks.text: He cites a Śaiva scripture claiming that attachment to limited religious knowledge prevents people from recognising the highest reality.
blocks.directed: He cites a Śaiva scripture claiming that attachment to limited religious knowledge prevents people from recognising the highest reality.

blocks.directed: Rather sectarian of him, isn’t it?

blocks.text: If your understanding of the ultimate is limited by the very categories you’re trying to transcend, you haven’t reached the ultimate.
blocks.directed: If your understanding of the ultimate is limited by the very categories you’re trying to transcend, you haven’t reached the ultimate.

blocks.text: If your religious worldview prevents you from investigating beyond its own boundaries, you’ve turned knowledge into another form of bondage.
blocks.directed: If your religious worldview prevents you from investigating beyond its own boundaries, you’ve turned knowledge into another form of bondage.

blocks.directed: And this is why you need three things.

blocks.text: Not just someone with an impressive beard.
blocks.directed: Not just someone with an impressive beard.

blocks.text: Not someone with thirty thousand followers and a particularly convincing photograph of themselves in the Himalayas.
blocks.directed: Not someone with thirty thousand followers and a particularly convincing photograph of themselves in the Himalayas.

blocks.text: Someone who can actually communicate the means of recognition.
blocks.directed: Someone who can actually communicate the means of recognition.

blocks.text: Because the point of the teaching is to transform your understanding until you recognise what was already true.
blocks.directed: Because the point of the teaching is to transform your understanding until you recognise what was already true.

blocks.text: Now, here’s where the philosophy gets really interesting.
blocks.directed: Now, here’s where the philosophy gets really interesting.

4. But can you really think your way into something beyond thought?
Ah.
blocks.directed:
4. But can you really think your way into something beyond thought?
Ah.

blocks.text: “You’ve just told me that I need to think correctly about the supreme reality.”

blocks.directed: [short pause] “But if I can think about it, surely it must be a concept?”

blocks.directed: The concept removes the mistaken understanding that prevents you from recognising the supreme reality.

blocks.directed: And even that analogy isn’t perfect, because the obstruction to recognising consciousness isn’t a genuinely independent thing.

blocks.directed: It’s a mistaken way of apprehending what’s already present.

blocks.directed: Correct understanding merely dispels the habitual impression that you’re separate from it.

blocks.directed: The breaking of the ingrained impression of duality.

blocks.text: And that’s the role of vikalpa.
blocks.directed: And that’s the role of vikalpa.

5. Some people are initiated by the goddesses themselves
Now, something fascinating.
blocks.directed:
5. Some people are initiated by the goddesses themselves
Now, something fascinating.

blocks.directed: For certain individuals, this discernment arises spontaneously.

blocks.directed: They’ve been struck by such an extraordinarily powerful descent of Śakti that they don’t require someone to sit them down and work through all the philosophical arguments.

blocks.directed: The appropriate understanding simply arises within them.

blocks.directed: [short pause] “Congratulations, you’re now officially qualified to recognise your own consciousness.”

blocks.text: The awakening has occurred through the divine powers themselves.
blocks.directed: The awakening has occurred through the divine powers themselves.

blocks.directed: But for others, this understanding develops through scripture and instruction.

blocks.directed: For now, let’s clarify what the teacher actually does.

blocks.directed: The scripture gives rise to correct understanding.

blocks.directed: That understanding leads to further correct understanding.

blocks.directed: One mistaken assumption collapses, exposing another.

blocks.directed: And this continuous process is called sat-tarka.

Right.

blocks.directed: The very reality through which you know any of these things?

blocks.directed: It’s the reality in which the meditator, meditation, and object of meditation all appear.

blocks.directed: What actually happens is that supreme consciousness, which has freely assumed the appearance of nonrecognition, progressively manifests itself more clearly.

Let’s begin with yāga.

blocks.directed: Remember the mirror from our last chapter?

blocks.text: Imagine a mirror containing an image of an elephant.
blocks.directed: Imagine a mirror containing an image of an elephant.

blocks.text: There’s an apparent difference between them.
blocks.directed: There’s an apparent difference between them.

blocks.text: But the elephant appearing in the mirror has no independent existence within that mirror apart from its reflective surface.
blocks.directed: But the elephant appearing in the mirror has no independent existence within that mirror apart from its reflective surface.

blocks.text: And here we have explicit differentiation.
blocks.directed: And here we have explicit differentiation.

blocks.text: You experience yourself as one thing.
blocks.directed: You experience yourself as one thing.

blocks.text: One object distinct from another object.
blocks.directed: One object distinct from another object.

blocks.text: Now, don’t imagine Aparā is somehow a rival goddess who’s gone rogue and started manufacturing an evil universe.
blocks.directed: Now, don’t imagine Aparā is somehow a rival goddess who’s gone rogue and started manufacturing an evil universe.

blocks.text: Differentiation is itself one of the powers of supreme consciousness.
blocks.directed: Differentiation is itself one of the powers of supreme consciousness.

blocks.text: So we’ve got three principal ways reality is apprehended.
blocks.directed: So we’ve got three principal ways reality is apprehended.

blocks.text:
14. The goddess who swallows all three
Right.
blocks.directed:
14. The goddess who swallows all three
Right.

blocks.text: Now what happens when consciousness draws all three modes back into itself?
blocks.directed: Now what happens when consciousness draws all three modes back into itself?

blocks.text: When even the distinction between these modes is absorbed?
blocks.directed: When even the distinction between these modes is absorbed?

blocks.text: We encounter a supreme, all-embracing power.
blocks.directed: We encounter a supreme, all-embracing power.

blocks.text: Also spoken of as Śrī Parā, in her transcendent aspect.
blocks.directed: Also spoken of as Śrī Parā, in her transcendent aspect.

blocks.text: And she possesses names such as:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And she possesses names such as:

blocks.text: The essential reality of the knowing subject.
blocks.directed: The essential reality of the knowing subject.

blocks.text: She who draws time into herself.
blocks.directed: She who draws time into herself.

blocks.text: Now that is a terrifyingly beautiful name.
blocks.directed: Now that is a terrifyingly beautiful name.

blocks.text: The ordering of things into before and after.
blocks.directed: The ordering of things into before and after.

blocks.text: The very field in which experiences arise, endure and disappear.
blocks.directed: The very field in which experiences arise, endure and disappear.

blocks.text: And here is the goddess who draws that entire process back into its own conscious source.
blocks.directed: And here is the goddess who draws that entire process back into its own conscious source.

blocks.text: Not because the universe is something disgusting that needs destroying.
blocks.directed: Not because the universe is something disgusting that needs destroying.

blocks.text: But because the totality of manifestation is never independent of her.
blocks.directed: But because the totality of manifestation is never independent of her.

blocks.text: All distinction can be gathered back into its supreme ground.
blocks.directed: All distinction can be gathered back into its supreme ground.

blocks.text: We have four fundamental aspects of Śakti.
blocks.directed: We have four fundamental aspects of Śakti.

blocks.text: And each can operate through three processes.
blocks.directed: And each can operate through three processes.

blocks.text: And this gives us the twelve Kālīs.
blocks.directed: And this gives us the twelve Kālīs.

blocks.text:
15. The twelve Kālīs — how consciousness devours its own universe
Now, before you imagine twelve enormous dark goddesses stomping across the cosmos, understand something.
blocks.directed:
15. The twelve Kālīs — how consciousness devours its own universe
Now, before you imagine twelve enormous dark goddesses stomping across the cosmos, understand something.

blocks.text: We’re investigating the actual process of awareness.
blocks.directed: We’re investigating the actual process of awareness.

blocks.text: These twelve powers can be understood as twelve moments in the activity of consciousness.
blocks.directed: These twelve powers can be understood as twelve moments in the activity of consciousness.

blocks.text: Before the thing becomes explicitly manifest, it takes shape within awareness.
blocks.directed: Before the thing becomes explicitly manifest, it takes shape within awareness.

blocks.text: The appearance becomes distinct and explicit.
blocks.directed: The appearance becomes distinct and explicit.

blocks.text: And consciousness takes an interest in it.
blocks.directed: And consciousness takes an interest in it.

blocks.text: A kind of fascination with its own manifestation.
blocks.directed: A kind of fascination with its own manifestation.

blocks.text: For a moment, consciousness becomes absorbed in the object.
blocks.directed: For a moment, consciousness becomes absorbed in the object.

blocks.text: And there’s delight in its appearing.
blocks.directed: And there’s delight in its appearing.

blocks.text: Consciousness begins to withdraw that appearance.
blocks.directed: Consciousness begins to withdraw that appearance.

blocks.text: The thing that seemed to stand before awareness begins to be reabsorbed.
blocks.directed: The thing that seemed to stand before awareness begins to be reabsorbed.

blocks.text: And consciousness generates this hesitation and consumes it.
blocks.directed: And consciousness generates this hesitation and consumes it.

blocks.text: The obstruction itself is another manifestation of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The obstruction itself is another manifestation of consciousness.

blocks.text: It doesn’t have some mysterious independent existence.
blocks.directed: It doesn’t have some mysterious independent existence.

blocks.text: With the hesitation consumed, the object is absorbed inward.
blocks.directed: With the hesitation consumed, the object is absorbed inward.

blocks.text: The thing that appeared separate is gathered back into awareness.
blocks.directed: The thing that appeared separate is gathered back into awareness.

blocks.text: Now consciousness recognises its own power of withdrawal.
blocks.directed: Now consciousness recognises its own power of withdrawal.

blocks.text: It apprehends that the capacity to dissolve appearances belongs to its nature.
blocks.directed: It apprehends that the capacity to dissolve appearances belongs to its nature.

blocks.text: “I am that within which its manifestation and disappearance occur.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am that within which its manifestation and disappearance occur.”

blocks.text: Now even the residual traces of the experience are considered.
blocks.directed: Now even the residual traces of the experience are considered.

blocks.text: Others are completely dissolved into pure consciousness.
blocks.directed: Others are completely dissolved into pure consciousness.

blocks.text: The experience is being withdrawn at increasingly subtle levels.
blocks.directed: The experience is being withdrawn at increasingly subtle levels.

blocks.text: The entire apparatus through which experiences arise is drawn inward.
blocks.directed: The entire apparatus through which experiences arise is drawn inward.

blocks.text: But the powers through which they’re known.
blocks.directed: But the powers through which they’re known.

blocks.text: Even the presiding principle of those faculties is withdrawn.
blocks.directed: Even the presiding principle of those faculties is withdrawn.

blocks.text: The lord of the instruments of cognition.
blocks.directed: The lord of the instruments of cognition.

blocks.text: Even that organising centre has no final independence.
blocks.directed: Even that organising centre has no final independence.

blocks.text: Now the limited subject itself is withdrawn.
blocks.directed: Now the limited subject itself is withdrawn.

blocks.text: “I am this person observing these things.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am this person observing these things.”

blocks.text: The subject formed under the conditions of māyā.
blocks.directed: The subject formed under the conditions of māyā.

blocks.text: Now there’s an extraordinary movement toward complete expansion.
blocks.directed: Now there’s an extraordinary movement toward complete expansion.

blocks.text: The subject that is no longer confined to ordinary individuality approaches unrestricted awareness.
blocks.directed: The subject that is no longer confined to ordinary individuality approaches unrestricted awareness.

blocks.text: Even this expanded knower is gathered back.
blocks.directed: Even this expanded knower is gathered back.

blocks.text: And finally, even the fully expanded manifestation is absorbed into the supreme ground.
blocks.directed: And finally, even the fully expanded manifestation is absorbed into the supreme ground.

blocks.text: Nothing remains as a separate entity standing over against consciousness.
blocks.directed: Nothing remains as a separate entity standing over against consciousness.

blocks.text: The process has returned to its source.
blocks.directed: The process has returned to its source.

blocks.text: This isn’t merely some cosmological story about what happens when the universe ends.
blocks.directed: This isn’t merely some cosmological story about what happens when the universe ends.

blocks.text: These twelve movements can occur within a single act of awareness.
blocks.directed: These twelve movements can occur within a single act of awareness.

blocks.text: The dissolution of the apparent object.
blocks.directed: The dissolution of the apparent object.

blocks.text: And ultimately the recognition of the conscious ground.
blocks.directed: And ultimately the recognition of the conscious ground.

blocks.text: Nor do these twelve movements have to arise one after another in a rigid sequence.
blocks.directed: Nor do these twelve movements have to arise one after another in a rigid sequence.

blocks.text: Across multiple subjects or within a single subject.
blocks.directed: Across multiple subjects or within a single subject.

blocks.text: And their pattern can be contemplated externally in larger cycles.
blocks.directed: And their pattern can be contemplated externally in larger cycles.

blocks.text: Or even smaller ritual arrangements involving pots, cloths and other objects.
blocks.directed: Or even smaller ritual arrangements involving pots, cloths and other objects.

blocks.text: All reflect patterns of manifestation, maintenance and withdrawal.
blocks.directed: All reflect patterns of manifestation, maintenance and withdrawal.

blocks.text: And these twelve goddesses are called:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And these twelve goddesses are called:

blocks.text: Because of the multiple meanings associated with kalana.
blocks.directed: Because of the multiple meanings associated with kalana.

blocks.text: She is not merely operating upon an already existing universe.
blocks.directed: She is not merely operating upon an already existing universe.

blocks.text: She is the very power through which the universe is manifested, known and reabsorbed.
blocks.directed: She is the very power through which the universe is manifested, known and reabsorbed.

blocks.text: My teacher Bhūtirāja explained this in terms of the goddess’s powers of projection and knowledge.
blocks.directed: My teacher Bhūtirāja explained this in terms of the goddess’s powers of projection and knowledge.

blocks.text: And there’s much more to be said.
blocks.directed: And there’s much more to be said.

blocks.text: I’ve explored these teachings in my other works.
blocks.directed: I’ve explored these teachings in my other works.

blocks.text: But there’s a reason I’m not putting every single esoteric detail in one place.
blocks.directed: But there’s a reason I’m not putting every single esoteric detail in one place.

blocks.text: My teachers taught me that the deepest secrets should neither be revealed all together nor concealed absolutely.
blocks.directed: My teachers taught me that the deepest secrets should neither be revealed all together nor concealed absolutely.

blocks.text: So that’s as far as we’re going here.
blocks.directed: So that’s as far as we’re going here.

blocks.text:
16. Stop treating limited gods as the absolute
Now, let’s return to our five practices.
blocks.directed:
16. Stop treating limited gods as the absolute
Now, let’s return to our five practices.

blocks.text: Everything I’ve explained must be understood in relation to this supreme Mahēśvara.
blocks.directed: Everything I’ve explained must be understood in relation to this supreme Mahēśvara.

blocks.text: Not merely a particular limited form somewhere within the hierarchy of reality.
blocks.directed: Not merely a particular limited form somewhere within the hierarchy of reality.

blocks.text: Now this is an important point.
blocks.directed: Now this is an important point.

blocks.text: Within our philosophical account, even the divine principles ranging from Viṣṇu to the tattva called Śiva are not to be mistaken, in their differentiated forms, for the unsurpassable absolute.
blocks.directed: Within our philosophical account, even the divine principles ranging from Viṣṇu to the tattva called Śiva are not to be mistaken, in their differentiated forms, for the unsurpassable absolute.

blocks.text: The highest reality isn’t merely one more item in a hierarchy.
blocks.directed: The highest reality isn’t merely one more item in a hierarchy.

blocks.text: It’s the very ground of the hierarchy.
blocks.directed: It’s the very ground of the hierarchy.

blocks.text: And the yogin seeking anuttara, the unsurpassable, must relinquish any understanding that mistakes a limited manifestation for the totality.
blocks.directed: And the yogin seeking anuttara, the unsurpassable, must relinquish any understanding that mistakes a limited manifestation for the totality.

blocks.text: My predecessor Vidyādhipati made a particularly forceful point about this in his Anubhavastotra.
blocks.directed: My predecessor Vidyādhipati made a particularly forceful point about this in his Anubhavastotra.

blocks.text: The supreme reality must not be reduced to some limited theological conception.
blocks.directed: The supreme reality must not be reduced to some limited theological conception.

blocks.text: It’s the living reality of experience itself.
blocks.directed: It’s the living reality of experience itself.

blocks.text: And as understanding becomes established, the practices should be undertaken in whatever form proves appropriate.
blocks.directed: And as understanding becomes established, the practices should be undertaken in whatever form proves appropriate.

blocks.text: And this is going to upset some very serious religious people.
blocks.directed: And this is going to upset some very serious religious people.

blocks.text:
17. Stop tormenting yourself over purity rules
Right.
blocks.directed:
17. Stop tormenting yourself over purity rules
Right.

blocks.text: Because apparently humans have developed an extraordinary talent for turning eating into a philosophical catastrophe.
blocks.directed: Because apparently humans have developed an extraordinary talent for turning eating into a philosophical catastrophe.
[short pause] “You can eat this on Tuesday.”

blocks.text: “Unless you’re performing this ceremony, in which case it’s suddenly fine.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Unless you’re performing this ceremony, in which case it’s suddenly fine.”

blocks.text: Let’s investigate what purity actually is.
blocks.directed: Let’s investigate what purity actually is.

blocks.text: Is purity an intrinsic property of an object?
blocks.directed: Is purity an intrinsic property of an object?

blocks.text: Under ordinary circumstances, its blueness is a property of the thing.
blocks.directed: Under ordinary circumstances, its blueness is a property of the thing.

blocks.text: Consider how the very same act can be declared permissible in one religious context and forbidden in another.
blocks.directed: Consider how the very same act can be declared permissible in one religious context and forbidden in another.

blocks.text: For example, a charitable donation might ordinarily be approved.
blocks.directed: For example, a charitable donation might ordinarily be approved.

blocks.text: Yet under particular Vedic sacrificial restrictions, an initiated individual may be forbidden from giving it.
blocks.directed: Yet under particular Vedic sacrificial restrictions, an initiated individual may be forbidden from giving it.

blocks.text: So has the donation itself physically transformed?
blocks.directed: So has the donation itself physically transformed?

blocks.text: Has something inside it suddenly become metaphysically contaminated?
blocks.directed: Has something inside it suddenly become metaphysically contaminated?

blocks.text: The difference comes from the applicable religious injunction.
blocks.directed: The difference comes from the applicable religious injunction.

blocks.text: “But Abhinava! Those rules are authoritative because the Veda says so!”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “But Abhinava! Those rules are authoritative because the Veda says so!”

blocks.text: But other scriptures prescribe different rules.
blocks.directed: But other scriptures prescribe different rules.

blocks.text: “Yes, but those don’t count because the Veda overrides them!”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Yes, but those don’t count because the Veda overrides them!”

blocks.text: And why exactly should that be accepted?
blocks.directed: And why exactly should that be accepted?

blocks.text: Within our Śaiva tradition, we hold that Śiva’s injunction possesses the overriding authority, supported by reasoning and scriptures such as the Sarvajñānottara.
blocks.directed: Within our Śaiva tradition, we hold that Śiva’s injunction possesses the overriding authority, supported by reasoning and scriptures such as the Sarvajñānottara.

blocks.text: So merely appealing to another injunction won’t settle the matter.
blocks.directed: So merely appealing to another injunction won’t settle the matter.

blocks.text: But the deeper issue for our present purpose is this:
blocks.directed: [short pause] But the deeper issue for our present purpose is this:

blocks.text: Purity and impurity, as ritual classifications, aren’t inherent features of objects in the way ordinary physical properties are.
blocks.directed: Purity and impurity, as ritual classifications, aren’t inherent features of objects in the way ordinary physical properties are.

blocks.text: They’re established through systems of conceptual distinction and prescription.
blocks.directed: They’re established through systems of conceptual distinction and prescription.

blocks.text: I’m not telling you that every action is equally wise, harmless or beneficial.
blocks.directed: I’m not telling you that every action is equally wise, harmless or beneficial.

blocks.text: We’re discussing the metaphysical status of ritual distinctions within the liberated vision.
blocks.directed: We’re discussing the metaphysical status of ritual distinctions within the liberated vision.

blocks.text: And at the level of practice we’re describing, the yogin should not exhaust himself through endless conceptual anxieties about what may be eaten, what may not, what is pure, and what is impure.
blocks.directed: And at the level of practice we’re describing, the yogin should not exhaust himself through endless conceptual anxieties about what may be eaten, what may not, what is pure, and what is impure.

blocks.text: These distinctions are not the supreme reality.
blocks.directed: These distinctions are not the supreme reality.

blocks.text: In fact, even the various prescriptions and prohibitions found throughout religious traditions — whether Vedic, Śaiva Siddhānta, tantric, Kula, or other systems — have no independent capacity to confer the final recognition we’re discussing.
blocks.directed: In fact, even the various prescriptions and prohibitions found throughout religious traditions — whether Vedic, Śaiva Siddhānta, tantric, Kula, or other systems — have no independent capacity to confer the final recognition we’re discussing.

blocks.text: They may have their functions in particular contexts.
blocks.directed: They may have their functions in particular contexts.

blocks.text: But they’re not the direct means here.
blocks.directed: But they’re not the direct means here.

blocks.text: The direct means remains clear discernment of the supreme nature of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The direct means remains clear discernment of the supreme nature of consciousness.

blocks.text: And the practitioner should approach the five practices in whatever manner actually cultivates that recognition.
blocks.directed: And the practitioner should approach the five practices in whatever manner actually cultivates that recognition.

blocks.text:
18. The final verses — you’re not the little creature you think you are
Let me tell you what the bound individual believes.
blocks.directed:
18. The final verses — you’re not the little creature you think you are
Let me tell you what the bound individual believes.
[short pause] From Abhinavagupta’s first concluding verse:

blocks.text: I am tied up by the bonds of karma.
blocks.directed: I am tied up by the bonds of karma.

blocks.text: I am driven about by something other than myself.
blocks.directed: I am driven about by something other than myself.

blocks.text: That’s the ordinary condition of the paśu.
blocks.directed: That’s the ordinary condition of the paśu.

blocks.text: These are not merely fleeting thoughts.
blocks.directed: These are not merely fleeting thoughts.

blocks.text: Fundamental certainties about what one is.
blocks.directed: Fundamental certainties about what one is.

blocks.text: The person has become utterly convinced of their own limitation.
blocks.directed: The person has become utterly convinced of their own limitation.

blocks.text: A conviction opposed to all these limiting understandings.
blocks.directed: A conviction opposed to all these limiting understandings.

blocks.text: And suppose it becomes firmly established.
blocks.directed: And suppose it becomes firmly established.

blocks.text: Then, says Abhinavagupta, the bound being immediately recognises the condition of the Lord.
blocks.directed: Then, says Abhinavagupta, the bound being immediately recognises the condition of the Lord.

blocks.text: Whose body is the entire universe.
blocks.directed: Whose body is the entire universe.

blocks.text: The transition from paśu to pati.
blocks.directed: The transition from paśu to pati.

blocks.text: From the apparent captive to the Lord.
blocks.directed: From the apparent captive to the Lord.

blocks.text: Not through manufacturing an entirely new consciousness.
blocks.directed: Not through manufacturing an entirely new consciousness.

blocks.text: But through the collapse of the mistaken understanding of what consciousness is.
blocks.directed: But through the collapse of the mistaken understanding of what consciousness is.

blocks.text: And the second verse gives the instruction.
blocks.directed: And the second verse gives the instruction.

blocks.text: However this correct conviction is attained, the supreme yogin should continually cultivate it.
blocks.directed: However this correct conviction is attained, the supreme yogin should continually cultivate it.

blocks.text: Don’t abandon it because somebody has come along with an impressive argument based on a mistaken conception of reality.
blocks.directed: Don’t abandon it because somebody has come along with an impressive argument based on a mistaken conception of reality.

blocks.text: Don’t allow your understanding to collapse merely because the world is full of contradictory opinions.
blocks.directed: Don’t allow your understanding to collapse merely because the world is full of contradictory opinions.

blocks.text: Examine things according to their actual nature.
blocks.directed: Examine things according to their actual nature.

blocks.text: And remain established in the understanding that reveals that nature correctly.
blocks.directed: And remain established in the understanding that reveals that nature correctly.

blocks.text: You saw that the reality of every experience is consciousness.
blocks.directed: You saw that the reality of every experience is consciousness.

blocks.text: You saw that consciousness is not something separate from your own essential nature.
blocks.directed: You saw that consciousness is not something separate from your own essential nature.

blocks.text: You saw that every apparent object, every action and every form of worship arises within that reality.
blocks.directed: You saw that every apparent object, every action and every form of worship arises within that reality.

blocks.text: And through correct discernment, the conviction of separateness is progressively overcome.
blocks.directed: And through correct discernment, the conviction of separateness is progressively overcome.

blocks.text: Until the very thought that you’re a captive loses its hold.
blocks.directed: Until the very thought that you’re a captive loses its hold.

blocks.text: The awareness within which the universe appears recognises itself as the supreme Lord.
blocks.directed: The awareness within which the universe appears recognises itself as the supreme Lord.

blocks.text: You haven’t obtained an entirely different Self.
blocks.directed: You haven’t obtained an entirely different Self.

blocks.text: Śiva, who freely appeared as the limited individual, recognises himself through Śakti, the very power by which he appeared limited.
blocks.directed: Śiva, who freely appeared as the limited individual, recognises himself through Śakti, the very power by which he appeared limited.

blocks.text: Using the power of understanding to bring the misunderstanding of separation to an end.
blocks.directed: Using the power of understanding to bring the misunderstanding of separation to an end.

The original narrative order is preserved, with some explanatory analogies added. The twelve Kālīs are retold as the twelve operations described in the chapter, without importing their separately attested individual names into Abhinavagupta’s prose.

blocks.text: The method of the limited individual: meditation, breath, subtle sound, and the actual yogic techniques.
